2026-08-01 (user lore): Voidborn ships are 'grown' — omniscience's hero image is genuinely asymmetric (octopus/jellyfish). BUT many Voidborn ships ARE symmetric (user): 38/50 recover ok, median mirror_residual 0.085 vs 0.063-0.075 other factions. Voidborn over-represents in failures (12/36, incl. 8 of the 14 aspect<0.8 suspects). Selection rule: per-ship metrics govern; Voidborn is only a weak prior that a weird solve may be a real grown shape, not a solver error.

2026-08-01 (user, triad eyeball over the full sheet): hero art has a dominant composition convention — the BOW faces screen-LEFT on most ships (triad +Y pinned screen-right pointed at the stern 'on most of them'). Candidate nose-disambiguation prior for the consuming half: bow = screen-left end of the projected long axis; exceptions include the ~15% stern-toward-camera shots already listed in view_anomalies.

2026-08-01 (user, selection-pattern insight): most 'recovered footprint' panel wins are ships with OUT-RIGGER NACELLE/ENGINE PODS — the footprint polygon preserves the hull-to-pod gap, while the 96-station w(t) envelope (and TripoSR smoothing) blob the pods back onto the body. The profile schema's concave[] flags mark which stations are split (gap exists) but the gap geometry itself is discarded — a consuming-half consideration: pod ships need the polygon (or per-station interval sets), not just the envelope.

2026-08-01 (user, mesh-improvement insight): many tripo wins would improve by SQUARING the out-jutting wide sections at the rear — TripoSR rounds off blocky engine housings; the wide bottom-third parts should be more rectangular. Candidate fusion post-process: flatten w(t) bumps to their local max (plateau snapping) within the wide rear region.

ASPECT-FLOOR RULING (2026-08-06): all 12 sub-0.8 rejections ruled via user eyeball + mesh/family cross-checks. Floor CORRECT on 9: syndicate, cogito, atmospheric_sampler, postulate, ice_dividend, aether, probable_cause, no_refunds (wrecked solves of elongated hulls — recurring causes: degenerate round/square cross-sections, stern-on receding poses) + close_enough (shape solved correctly, only beam scale disputed, 0.72 vs mesh-adj 1.85). Floor WRONG on 3: apeiron, qualia, vigil — ALL voidborn batwing/crescent wings, where the squat measurement is real and TripoSR's aspect is span-inverted. RULING: keep ASPECT_BOUNDS floor at 0.8 as the MoGe gate (9-for-12); fusion adds a voidborn-wing exception — trust pipeline aspect + polygon for crescents, never mesh aspect. Squaring (snap_plateaus) is a PER-SHIP choice: helps ice_dividend, hurts postulate — arbitrated by mesh067/mesh067sq picks.

RECEDING-POSE MARKER (2026-08-06, user): most ships clicked at 2 o'clock have the bow pointing back and AWAY from the camera — the mirror composition that points up-right also points into depth. Verified: of the 15 two-o'clock ships, the only 2 failures are no_refunds + probable_cause, exactly the stern-on foreshortening wrecks from the floor ruling, both at the cohort-low 0.81 alignment; cohort median alignment 0.93 vs 1.00 for the 8/4-o'clock groups. A 2-o'clock bow click is a cheap prior for 'length axis foreshortened, treat the pipeline aspect with suspicion' — useful fusion signal.

FOOTPRINT-PICK SEMANTICS (2026-08-06, user): every 'recovered footprint' best-pick (26 ships: analysis, brain_freeze, chop_shop, consensus, deep_resonance, dialectic, dimensional_fold, dissolution, four_on_the_floor, gas_tanker, good_enough, interstice, liability, maul, midlife_crisis, need_to_know, permafrost, portfolio, premiere, prospectus, repo, siege_breaker, substrate, thermodynamic_end, treasury, warranty) was chosen because the polygon captured some smaller detail that the profile w(t) smoothed or flattened — the envelope's station-averaging erases fine features beyond just pod gaps. Fusion rule: a footprint pick means publish from the POLYGON; more generally, high-frequency boundary content in the polygon that w(t) lacks is a detail-loss signal, not noise. Canonical example of the lost detail (user): wingtips with large protruding blasters, X-wing style — the polygon keeps the tip cannons, the station-averaged envelope flattens them.

UNPICKED = TOUGH SHAPES (2026-08-06, user hypothesis, verified): the 95 ships with no best-pick skew toward shapes no method got right (user-named examples: interstice, omniscience, paradox). By faction unpicked rate: voidborn 56% (28/50, worst — organic curves/protrusions: omniscience, fugue, nebulous, rift_siphon, the wing/crescent family), outerrim 44% (greebled junkers), crimson 35%, nebula 31%, solarian 23%, pirate 15% (easiest). Unpicked voidborn also have the worst median mirror residual (0.077 vs 0.065 for picked voidborn). Fusion implication: absence of a pick is itself a signal — low confidence in ALL candidates, flag for mesh-first or manual handling rather than silently publishing the least-bad one.

FRONT-PRONG FAILURE MODE (2026-08-06, user): another common reason for no best-pick — ships with two protrusions/prongs at the BOW. No candidate captures them: w(t) welds the gap shut (split cross-sections), the mesh smooths them, and the alpha shape may bridge the fork. Detectable from data: nose-first profiles whose concave flags concentrate in the front third (candidates: manifest_destiny, yard_sale, ice_dividend, no_refunds, last_call, reclaim, junk_convoy, insurance_fraud, repo, losers_weepers, bedrock, aether, theorem, finders_keepers, ordinance, noumenon, appraisal, glows_in_the_dark, warhammer, paradox, vigil, baling_wire, entropy). Same structural root as pod-blobbing — the envelope cannot represent disjoint cross-sections — so the fix is the same: publish the POLYGON for prong ships, and the glyph/footprint consumer must respect concave[] stations at the bow. USER-CONFIRMED prong ships (2026-08-06): crucible, annihilator, encyclopedia, apeiron (little prongs), frankenhauler — NONE were in the concave-flag candidate list, so small prongs get bridged by the alpha shape before the envelope sees a split; the detector only catches big forks. frankenhauler: the recovered footprint polygon gets closest of any candidate — consistent with polygon-for-prongs.

receding_pose_ships_2026-08-06._desc: User-identified (2026-08-06): hero art points these ships AWAY from camera away from camera — one batch toward 2-3 o'clock (bow up-right into depth), a mirror batch toward 9-10 o'clock (bow up-left into depth; see ships_away_left). Same idiom-name family, likely one art batch's shared composition templates. Consequence: the length axis is foreshortened, so pipeline aspect is systematically UNDER-measured for the whole cohort — outright wrecking no_refunds (0.59), probable_cause (0.49), and running_tab (low-obliquity withdrawal), and shading the rest low even where the solve passed. Treat pipeline aspect as a lower bound here; prefer mesh/family aspect for scale.
